The Analyst Behind
the Numbers

Turning raw BFSI data into business decisions — with precision, compliance, and clarity.

I am a Data Analyst at Tata Consultancy Services with 2.5+ years of hands-on experience in the BFSI domain, operating within the TCS BaNCS policy administration and financial reporting ecosystem.

My work centers on designing 25+ operational and regulatory SQL reports, executing ETL pipelines across multiple source systems, and maintaining 99%+ data accuracy across 50K+ records through systematic validation and reconciliation workflows.

I build and maintain Power BI MIS dashboards that translate complex financial data into executive-ready KPI views — while leveraging Power Query automation to cut manual reporting effort significantly.

Recognized with three TCS awards — Xcelerate Warrior, Certificate of Appreciation, and On The Spot — for performance excellence, compliance delivery, and project contribution in high-stakes BFSI environments.

Project 04  ·  BFSI Credit Risk Analytics
Lending Club Loan Portfolio Analytics
Power BI >Python · Pandas · NumPy SQL · SQLite Credit Risk
GitHub
Business Problem

A lending institution lacked visibility into portfolio risk, borrower behavior, recovery performance, and geographic lending exposure. The objective was to identify high-risk loan segments, measure default drivers, and build an executive reporting solution for portfolio monitoring and credit risk management.

Analytical Approach

Built an end-to-end credit risk analytics solution using a 225K-record sample from Lending Club's 2M+ loan dataset. Engineered risk-focused features including default flags, risk tiers, DTI bands, recovery rates, employment stability, and income segmentation using Python. Developed 10 analytical SQL queries and delivered a 3-page interactive Power BI dashboard with executive, risk, and geographic reporting views.

Impact Metrics

Key Business Insights
Grade G loans default at 40.43% compared to only 3.36% for Grade A loans, revealing a 12× risk differential and confirming loan grade as the strongest predictor of default.
Borrowers with DTI between 30–40 default at 15.92%, nearly double the rate of low-DTI borrowers, highlighting debt burden as a major credit risk factor.
Debt consolidation represents 59.81% of portfolio volume, exposing the institution to concentration risk within a single lending category.
Recovery rate remains below 1%, indicating significant credit-loss exposure and limited post-default capital recovery.

Project 05  ·  Financial Data Engineering & Analytics
Automated Stock Market ETL & Analytics Pipeline
Power BI Python · ETL SQL · SQLite Financial Analytics
GitHub
Business Problem

Financial market data is generated continuously across exchanges, making manual collection and analysis inefficient. The objective was to automate stock data ingestion, transformation, and reporting while providing actionable insights into stock performance, technical indicators, and market trends across Indian and US BFSI sectors.

Analytical Approach

Designed and implemented an end-to-end automated ETL pipeline that extracted, transformed, and loaded 1,700+ stock market records for 7 BFSI stocks from NSE and NYSE into SQLite. Engineered 14 technical indicators including RSI, Moving Averages, Volatility, Cumulative Returns, and Buy/Sell signals using Python. Built analytical SQL models and delivered a 3-page Power BI dashboard for stock analysis, portfolio monitoring, and India vs USA market comparison.

// sql showcase

SQL at Scale

Production-grade queries delivering BFSI reports, KPIs, and ETL transformations at TCS.

kpi_revenue_report.sql
-- KPI Revenue Reporting Query (BFSI) SELECT p.policy_id, p.customer_id, SUM(t.premium_amount) AS total_premium, COUNT(t.transaction_id) AS txn_count, ROUND( SUM(t.premium_amount) / COUNT(t.transaction_id), 2 ) AS avg_transaction FROM policies p JOIN transactions t ON p.policy_id = t.policy_id WHERE t.status = 'ACTIVE' AND t.txn_date >= DATEADD( month, -12, GETDATE() ) GROUP BY p.policy_id, p.customer_id ORDER BY total_premium DESC;
customer_segmentation.sql
-- Customer Segmentation & RFM Analysis WITH rfm AS ( SELECT customer_id, DATEDIFF(day, MAX(order_date), GETDATE()) AS recency, COUNT(order_id) AS frequency, SUM(order_value) AS monetary FROM customer_orders GROUP BY customer_id ) SELECT *, CASE WHEN frequency > 10 AND monetary > 5000 THEN 'High Value' WHEN recency < 30 THEN 'Active' ELSE 'At Risk' END AS segment FROM rfm ORDER BY monetary DESC;
